clues.title: Coverage: only the capital
text: Uganda has **very limited **coverage, with most of the coverage in the capital city of Kampala and the nearby city of Entebbe. The rest of the coverage is located in the various national parks that will be covered below.

Note: Because the coverage in Uganda is limited, this guide is structured differently than most of the other country guides, with two separate sections for Kampala and the National Parks. These sections also include most of the tips needed to identify the country.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: Coverage is very limited: mostly the capital and a nearby city, plus a few national parks. Most clues come from those places.

clues.title: Driving side: left
text: Uganda drives on the **left hand** side of the road.

NOTE: African countries are split between right and left hand drive. For a full overview of countries and their driving side, see [here](https://www.plonkit.net/images/beginners-guide/Driving_direction_v11.png).

images.caption: Traffic driving on the left, with a two-way traffic warning sign

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the left. Africa is split between left and right, so this helps narrow it down.

clues.title: Plate: white front, yellow rear
text: Uganda uses **white **front plates with **yellow **rear plates. These plates can be long or tall.

images.caption: Ugandan plates: front, rear long and rear high

clues.summary: White plate on the front of the car, yellow on the back. Plates can be long or tall.

clues.title: Google car: white, boxy, square mirrors
text: In all coverage in Kampala, a unique Google car is visible. This car is **white** with **square **side mirrors and a boxy look.
NOTE: This Google car is only found in Uganda and is unique to the city of Kampala and its outskirts.
clues.summary: In the capital the car is white and boxy, with square side mirrors. This car exists nowhere else.

clues.title: Streets: busy, unpaved, walled houses
text: Kampala is a fairly **busy-looking** city, with many signs, narrow **unpaved **roads and typically fairly small, one-storey houses. Like many African countries, houses will often be surrounded by tall walls, commonly with barbed wire on top.
clues.summary: A busy city with lots of signs, narrow unpaved roads and small one-storey houses. Houses sit behind tall walls, often topped with barbed wire.

clues.title: Soil: very red, even under the tarmac
text: Like most of the national park coverage, Kampalan soil is typically very **red**. Even paved roads normally have a noticeable red, purple or pink tinge.
clues.summary: The soil is deep red. Even paved roads often look slightly red, purple or pink.

clues.title: Landscape: hilly city
text: Kampala is a very **hilly **city, and as such it is rare to get a round without elevation or noticeable hills.
clues.summary: The capital is very hilly. It is rare to get a round there without noticeable slopes.

clues.title: Vehicles: taxi vans with blue blocky pattern
text: Throughout Kampala, you will often see these **taxi buses**, with a blue blocky pattern on the sides. These are a good clue for the city if you are not able to see the Google car.

images.caption: Taxi van with a blue blocky pattern along its side; the circle at left shows the pattern

clues.summary: Minibus taxis with a blue blocky pattern on the sides are everywhere in the capital. Useful if the Google car is not visible.

clues.title: Streets: rich city centre, black-white curbs
text: In the **city centre** of Kampala, you will see paved roads with black-and-white curbs. In contrast to the rest of the city, the city centre looks richer and very built-up, with lots of multi-storey buildings.
clues.summary: The city centre has paved roads with black-and-white curbs and many multi-storey buildings. It looks much richer than the rest of the city.

clues.title: Streets: emptier, greener, more street signs
text: The city of Entebbe, southwest of Kampala, can often be recognized by feeling slightly emptier than most of the capital, with more **greenery **and somewhat fancier houses. The area also has significantly more **street signs** than the rest of the capital.

images.caption: Red dirt road fork; the circle at bottom left zooms on a Park Lane street sign

clues.summary: A city south-west of the capital. It feels emptier and greener, with nicer houses and many more street signs.

clues.title: Google car: boxy car with black front bar
text: Most coverage in the Ugandan national parks was taken with this Street View car, which is similar to the one seen in Kampala, but with a** black bar** along the front of the car. The visibility of the car varies greatly, and it is somewhat common for it to not be visible at all.
clues.summary: Most park coverage uses a car like the capital one, but with a black bar across the front. Sometimes the car is not visible at all.

clues.title: Landscape: savannah ringed by mountains
text: The National Park is located in the northeastern parts of the country and mostly consists of a large savannah with **mountains** being visible in most directions. The most recognizable mountain range can be seen to the east and is visible in most of the coverage.
clues.summary: In the north-east, a big savannah with mountains in almost every direction. The most recognisable range is to the east.

clues.title: Landscape: wooded road, hidden mountains
text: The southern half of the north road in Kidepo is somewhat **forested**, and as such it may occasionally be hard to see the various mountains.
clues.summary: On the southern half of the north road, there are more trees, so the mountains are sometimes hard to see.

clues.title: Landscape: savannah with one wide mountain north
text: The northern half of the north road in Kidepo is located in a savannah and can be easily recognised by the **wide mountain** to the north.
clues.summary: On the northern half of the north road, open savannah with a wide mountain to the north.

clues.title: Guardrail: low dirt barriers, savannah and bushes
text: The National Park is located by the northern end of Lake Albert and can commonly be recognized by the low** dirt barriers** along the side of the roads. A savannah can be seen in the western part, while the eastern parts contain many small trees and bushes. Apart from a fairly low and wide mountain range far away to the west, there are no mountains in the vicinity.
clues.summary: Low dirt barriers along the roadside. Savannah to the west, small trees and bushes to the east. No mountains nearby, only a low wide range far west.

clues.title: Plants: distinctive palms, far north of a park
text: Seeing these **palms** in Uganda means you are extremely likely to be in the northern parts of Murchison Falls.
clues.summary: These palms mean you are very likely in the northern part of a park by the north end of a big lake.

clues.title: Road: very wide dirt road through tropical forest
text: The National Park has three types of coverage, the first of which is a very **wide dirt road** going through a dense, tropical forest. It is by far the widest dirt road in the country outside of Kampala with Street View coverage.
clues.summary: One of three coverage types in a forest park: a very wide dirt road through dense tropical forest. It is the widest dirt road with coverage outside the capital.

clues.title: Road: small forest road, flat and fairly bright
text: The second type of coverage in Kibale is on a **small forest road**, which is still large enough to be covered using a car. The forest appears to be quite dense, however it is typically not very dark. The area is mostly flat.
clues.summary: Second type in the forest park: a smaller road still wide enough for a car. The forest is dense but not very dark, and the land is flat.

clues.title: Road: tiny dark forest paths
text: The final type of coverage is a number of **tiny forest paths**. The coverage is somewhat dark, with the sun shining through every so often.
clues.summary: Third type in the forest park: narrow forest paths. Fairly dark, with sun shining through here and there.

clues.title: Landscape: the driest country coverage, hilly
text: The park is located west of lake Victoria and has by far the **driest coverage** in the country. The grass is almost always completely dried out, which is normally enough to recognise it. Bushes and trees along the road also typically look very dry. The area is quite hilly, but not mountainous.
clues.summary: West of Lake Victoria, the grass is almost always totally dried out. Bushes and trees look dry too. Hilly but not mountainous.

clues.title: Coverage: humid forest paths, drops on lens
text: The coverage in the national park consists of two small forest paths running parallel to each other. The forest appears very humid, and on much of the coverage, **drops of water** can be seen on the camera lens.

images.caption: Humid forest path; the red circle at lower left highlights water drops on the lens

clues.summary: Two small forest paths running side by side. The forest is very humid and water drops often show on the camera lens.

clues.title: Soil: forest path climbing east, dark red dirt
text: The national park is located near the Kenyan border and has two stretches of paths covered, the first of which is in a **forest **with a fairly steep slope heading upwards to the east. The dirt typically has a very dark red colour.
clues.summary: Near the Kenyan border, the first path runs through forest on a steep slope going up to the east. The dirt is a very dark red.

clues.title: Coverage: open hill, small palms, armed man
text: The eastern stretch of path covered is easily recognized by its small **palm-like** trees on an open hilly field and a man following the photographer, who is dressed in green and holding a **rifle**.
clues.summary: The eastern path is an open hilly field with small palm-like trees. A man in green holding a rifle walks behind the photographer.

clues.title: Soil: brown or greyish, not red
text: Queen Elizabeth National Park, north of Lake Edward, is one of the only places in Uganda where you will commonly see dirt which is **not red**. Instead, the dirt will typically be either **brown **or **greyish**.

images.caption: A dirt road with brown or greyish soil, not red

clues.summary: North of a big lake in the west, one of the few places where the dirt is brown or grey instead of red.

clues.title: Plants: tall branching cacti like trees
text: On top of the brown dirt, the national park also contains **large cacti** with many branches going almost straight upwards, resembling the shape of trees.
clues.summary: On top of brown soil, big cacti with many branches growing almost straight up, shaped like trees.

clues.title: Landscape: large water-filled craters
text: On the northern coverage, it is common to see large, **water-filled craters**. Similar craters cannot be found elsewhere in the country.
clues.summary: In the northern coverage, large craters filled with water are common. They are not found anywhere else in the country.

clues.title: Road: only paved road outside the capital
text: The **only paved road** with coverage outside Kampala can be found here. The pavement almost entirely lacks the red tinge which is typical for most roads in the country. The road has white, solid outer lines and a yellow middle line.
A power line runs parallel to the road, to your east. To your north, you will be able to see hills.
clues.summary: The only paved road with coverage outside the capital. No red tinge, white solid edge lines and a yellow centre line. Power line to the east, hills north.

clues.title: Coverage: the only big village outside the capital
text: **Katwe village** is the only significant settlement outside of Kampala with Street View coverage.
NOTE: Much smaller villages, safari lodges and single houses with coverage can be found elsewhere.
clues.summary: One village is the only significant settlement with coverage outside the capital. Smaller villages, lodges and single houses are covered elsewhere.
